To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distance between receptor dimers in kinase-active receptor complexes is not consistent with the distances found in the crystal structure of the isolated receptor fragment, but is consistent with the distance found in the crystal structures of receptor fragments in complex with the kinase CheA and CheW.

the interdimer distance in kinase-active signaling complexes of chemoreceptor dimers does not agree with the interdimer distances in two crystal structures, and that this finding provides constraints for possible receptor arrangements in signaling complexes.
the interdimer distance observed in the two crystal structures of chemoreceptor signaling domains does not exist in kinase-active signaling complexes of chemoreceptor dimers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the bacterial chemotaxis receptor signaling complexes.
the structure of the bacterial chemoreceptor dimer, and its role in the formation of the signaling complex.
the structure of bacterial signaling complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neither of the two models proposed to explain the packing of the receptor cytoplasm is correct.
the receptor dimer dimer contacts observed in crystal structure are not part of the signaling complex in solution.
the crystal structures do not provide an accurate description of the receptor-receptor interface in the signaling arrays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinase-active signaling complexes of chemoreceptors do contain the receptor-receptor contacts proposed by the crystal structures but do not contain the proposed receptor-receptor interfaces.
the crystal structures of receptor fragments are not a good guide for the arrangement of the signaling complexes that are active in bacterial chemotaxis.
kinase-active signaling complexes of chemoreceptors do contain the proposed receptor-receptor interactions but do not have the receptor-receptor distances that are predicted from crystal structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinase-active complexes of chemoreceptors do contain receptor dimers, but these are not in contact with each other as in the trimers of dimers or the hedgerow model.

the crystal structures of receptor signaling domains, while providing a wealth of information on the structure of the individual domains, cannot be used to model the arrangement of receptors in the signaling arrays.
